transcript.text: quick q: churn with 3% positives, should i report PR-AUC or ROC-AUC to my manager, and why? no data work, just the answer

Report **PR-AUC**, and add one number next to it. Why: with only a small slice of positives, the ROC curve has a huge flow of non-churners to lean on, so a model can score well there while still catching very few of the customers you actually wanted to find. Precision and recall look only at the positives, so PR-AUC is honest about imbalance. Two caveats: PR-AUC's baseline is your churn rate itself (the person's 3%), so anything near it means no skill and beating it by a wide margin is real signal; and it isn't comparable across months if the churn rate drifts, so keep ROC-AUC as a secondary trend number. For your manager, the line that lands is recall at the outreach list size you can actually afford, set against that same 3% baseline.
